Why it holds: when the real system lands in the support of Θ, the policy has already seen a similar θ during training, so it does not depend on a single guessed value.

Why it holds: the model learns nonlinear physics that hand-coded simulators miss (contact, deformation, friction regimes), and the denoising objective encourages the model to capture the central tendency of dynamics rather than memorizing noise.

Why it holds: the student model learns to read visual features that are predictive of true dynamics; the shared action space closes the teacher-student gap, so the visual policy generalizes better than training on images alone.

Physically Embodied Gaussian Splatting.work: A scene is captured as color images and depth; rendering alone (Gaussians) does not ground physics. Physically Embodied Gaussian Splatting represents the scene as both particles (small rigid bodies for collision) and Gaussians (alpha-blended ellipsoids for rendering). Pushing a toy block in the real scene: invert the Gaussians to find particle poses, simulate the push in a learned or hand-tuned physics engine, update Gaussian positions to match sim, and render the prediction. On a sequence of eight real pushes, the hybrid model generates physically consistent videos where predicted trajectories match real block motion within ≤ 2 cm error, enabling downstream sim-to-real transfer.

The move: optimize both jointly: physics loss on particle dynamics, rendering loss on splat output; keep particles and gaussians synchronized via μi = Xi. Why it holds: particles accurately simulate deformation and contact, while gaussians provide photorealistic appearance; jointly optimizing ties rendering artifacts to physical plausibility, avoiding divergence.

Why it holds: once an observation is converted to sim space, the sim-trained grasp policy applies directly; the mapping absorbs sensor noise and lighting differences, so the policy sees cleaner state than raw pixels.
